public_rationale: The claim says paying users will at some point face misbehaving models, a rate-limit shift, or a cost-driven change in functionality. Any one of these counts. Three weeks after the post, Anthropic changed weekly Claude Code limits across its Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans. Against what subscribers had, this was a 17% cut, and Anthropic itself acknowledged that figure. Reporting tied Anthropic's limit troubles to its rising costs. That is a dated rate-limit shift for paying users of a major LLM service, which meets the early resolution rule. There are caveats. The cut ended a temporary boost, and limits stayed 25% above the original baseline.
limitations: Evidence is secondary reporting, not Anthropic's own post.
The cost link is the reporter's framing.
The claim's 'guaranteed' covers every paying user; this shows it for one large service.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Paying users of LLM-powered services are guaranteed at some point to face service degradation where models misbehave, shifts in rate limits, or changes in product functionality driven by the services' shifting economics.

statement.excerpt: As a paying user of an LLM-powered service, you are guaranteed at some point to face a degradation in service where models misbehave, some sort of shift in rate limits, or some sort of change in product functionality based on their shifting economics.

from_speaker: As a paying user of an LLM-powered service
a degradation in service where models misbehave
some sort of shift in rate limits
or some sort of change in product functionality
our_interpretation: Plain reading: people who pay for major LLM services will, at some point, run into at least one of three things. Models misbehaving, a change in rate limits, or a change in what the product does, driven by the vendor's costs.
The claim is disjunctive, so one clear instance of any of the three on a major paid service counts as the forecast coming true for those users.
Only events after the post date (2026-08-25) count as outcome evidence.
criteria.support_condition: A documented change after the post to rate limits or functionality for paying users of a major LLM service, linked to the vendor's costs or economics. Or a documented degradation in model behavior for paying users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Major paid LLM services keeping limits, functionality and model behavior stable for paying users over a long period, with no cost-driven changes.

evidence.excerpt: Because the usage limit for Claude Code is currently 50 percent higher, you will lose out starting September 14. You will indeed have a higher limit than a few months ago, but compared to today, you lose exactly 17 percent.
evidence.explanation: Paying Claude users had their weekly Claude Code limits cut 17% from current levels after the post. That is a shift in rate limits.

evidence.excerpt: Starting September 14, Anthropic is raising the standard weekly usage limits for Claude Code by a permanent 25% across Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans.
evidence.locator: section 'What is actually changing with Claude Code’s rate limits?', paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: Confirms the change applied across all of Anthropic's paid plans and replaced a higher temporary limit, so subscribers faced a rate-limit shift.

evidence.excerpt: This is frustrating for users who hit their limit quickly, but also for Anthropic, which sees its costs skyrocketing.
evidence.explanation: The report ties Anthropic's limit management to its rising costs, which fits 'based on their shifting economics'. This is the reporter's framing, not Anthropic's stated reason.

evidence.excerpt: The doubled 5-hour session limits from May are not going away, only the weekly limit boost is being rolled back.
evidence.locator: section 'What’s staying the same or improving despite the cut?', paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: The cut was the end of a temporary promotion, and other limits stayed higher than before. That narrows how severe the change was.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: A cut to rate limits after the post, applied across all of a major LLM service's paid plans (Claude Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise), with reporting that links it to the vendor's rising costs.
